Darwin completion observation is registered only after process start. A fast child can exit before kqueue registration, causing ESRCH, a fallback process-group EPERM, and a failed cleanup result for an ordinary successful exit. The diagnostic and repeated focused and race suites reproduced the defect.

The required full shuffled Go test failed on a fast successful goal, and repeated shuffled focused and race suites also failed. Passing single-run race, vet, lint, generation, and cross-build receipts do not satisfy the all-required-checks condition.

The author-distinct validator consumed the exact repair intent, verified the frozen repository-wide subject and active epoch-1 contract, mapped all thirteen parent and repair criteria to typed receipts, and preserved the prior FAIL.

subprocess.Result now carries typed not-started, completed, and failed cleanup outcomes. The focused subprocess suite passed repeatedly, and the diagnostic retained an explicit attempted, incomplete, failed outcome with bounded detail.

The repair preserves typed terminal and cleanup error identities by joining them. The diagnostic retained the completion-observation, process-group signal, and parent-observation failures together instead of shadowing them.
Structured cleanup facts passed the repeated schema/output suite, and the goals-level diagnostic exposed the typed failed cleanup state and full diagnostic at the migrated caller boundary.

The required ordinary-success behavior is not deterministic on Darwin: concurrent fast exit-zero children are reported as cleanup failures. A single isolated replay can pass, but the dedicated concurrent diagnostic and repeated focused and race suites fail.
The prior FAIL is immutable and the fresh exact validation requirement is met, but the required full Go test and repeated race checks do not remain green.

findings.summary: Darwin registers EVFILT_PROC NOTE_EXIT after starting the child. When a fast child exits first, registration returns ESRCH; fallback signaling can return EPERM, and an ordinary exit-zero process is misclassified as failed cleanup.
The cleanup repair does not satisfy its no-regression gate because the required full shuffled test and repeated focused race suites fail on the same fast-success lifecycle defect.
